newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom cites high individual share orders.
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom cites high individual share orders.

text.p: Nearly one and a half million German private investors have placed firm orders to buy at least 100 shares in Deutsche Telekom when the German phone giant goes public next week, the company said on Tuesday.
The enormous demand will guarantee that the $12 billion issue is oversubscribed several times, market sources said.

Around 3.1 million Germans signed up with the company's share information centre (AIF) to take advantage of discounted share prices and loyalty bonuses for holding shares three years. Nearly half of these have now placed orders.
"We are in the range of our expectations with orders from 40 to 50 percent of the AIF participants," Telekom spokesman Hans Ehnert told Reuters.
Orders for shares can be placed until Thursday. The company will float up to 690 million shares. Trade begins in Germany and New York on November 18 and a day later in Tokyo.
Around 70 percent of shares will be placed in Germany and divided up between individual and institutional investors.
